claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in HEAs designed for fusion plasma-facing components are primarily governed by competition between dislocation slip and creep.
Dynamic strain aging modulates the competition between dislocation slip and creep.
Lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion induce dynamic strain aging in these HEAs.
Dynamic strain aging temporarily pins dislocations at high temperatures.
Temporary dislocation pinning improves toughness by controlling strain-rate sensitivity.
Deformation above approximately 0.6Tm at selected strain rates will activate dynamic strain aging.
The relevant structural mediator is transient dislocation pinning by lattice distortions and dynamically formed solute atmospheres.
High configurational entropy produces significant lattice distortion at elevated temperatures.
The combination of lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion permits dynamic strain aging.
Dynamic strain aging enhances effective plastic strain and toughness by balancing ductile slip against creep-controlled deformation rates.
Conditions promoting dynamic strain aging will produce higher fracture toughness than the baseline deformation condition.
Conditions promoting dynamic strain aging will alter strain-rate sensitivity and may produce a nonlinear stress-strain response with a plateau or flow-stress peak.
At the standard industrial strain rate selected as the baseline, traditional dislocation motion will dominate without significant dynamic strain aging.
The proposed mechanism is limited to high-temperature and strain-rate regimes in which lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion are important.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to conventional alloys.
